name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Lasher's dominant fundraising and outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certain
model.rationale: This Manhattan-based seat leans Democratic by 33 points, and Micah Lasher has raised over $3.3 million with more than $10 million in outside support, dwarfing Republican Caroline Shinkle's $155,000. Markets price a Democratic win at 98 percent, so the only real question is the size of the margin.
model.watch: A sharp national Republican wave or unexpectedly low Democratic turnout in a low-profile open seat could narrow the margin, though not realistically the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Manhattan and Brooklyn seat open, but the district's D+33 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold the strong default. Micah Lasher enters the general with a decisive financial edge, having raised $3.3 million and benefited from roughly $10.8 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000 with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability at 98 percent.

Two minor independent candidates poll negligible support. With no public polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals and money, both of which point firmly to Lasher. The expected margin is around 28 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
